item.title: The Bike Garage Open Hours: Woodland Location — Sat Sep 5, 9:00 AM — Bike Garage Woodland
item.description:
Woodland location: 1st and Hays streets at Douglass Middle School
FREE Bike Repair
Come to the Bike Garage, where our volunteer mechanics will repair your bike. We accept cash, Venmo, and Paypal donations. Interested in becoming a volunteer bike mechanic? No experience is necessary.
CONTACT US TO VOLUNTEER
Quality Used Bikes for SaleLowest prices on the best used bikes.Our inventory changes every day!
Hybrid bikes, town bikes, vintage bikes, road bikes, mountain bikes, kids’ bikes, and more. Visit the Bike Garage in Davis or Woodland to check out our inventory.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Open Studio — Sat Sep 5, 1:00 PM — Bubblegum Art Studio
item.description:
At open studio, you can use your imagination to make and art piece at our new creation station, play with playdough, make pony bead animals or fuse bead shapes, work on one of our many rotating projects, or purchase a base to paint, decorate and bedazzle! Fun for all ages, but best for ages 3-12 $20 per child
Source: The Dirt

item.title: September Art Spark: Fabric Mosaic — Sat Sep 5, 1:00 PM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Embrace your creativity at the Manetti Shrem Museum’s Carol and Gerry Parker Art Studio with an afternoon of art making inspired by works on view. Stop by the studio in September September: Fabric Mosaic Try out kinusaiga, a no-sew form of quilting, to create geometric patterns inspired by Woody De Othello’s ceramic mosaic works. No Art Spark on September 19 during special Orientation programming for UC Davis’ first-year students.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Sat Sep 5, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Sep 6, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
Experience the heart and soul of Davis every Saturday at the Davis Farmers Market in Central Park! 🗓 Every Saturday⏰ 8:00 AM – 1:00 PM📍 Central Park, Davis Shop fresh from the source with local farmers and vendors offering: 🥕 Fresh, seasonal produce🌻 Farm products🛍 Handmade crafts🥖 Fresh-baked goods☕ Coffee and hot food Whether you’re stocking up on locally grown ingredients, enjoying breakfast in the park, or simply soaking in the vibrant community atmosphere, the Davis Farmers Market is a beloved weekly tradition for all ages. Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Nov 11, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone
Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers

All are welcome to attend this free event that coincides with the downtown Woodland First Friday event. This exhibition celebrates the creative spaces of Yolo County Resident Artists. This non-juried exhibition is open to the first 30 Artists who deliver their artwork to Gallery 625, and each participating Artist will have an artwork and a photo of themselves in their studio on display. item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Sep 5, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Nov 18, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: Thursday Live! The Evie Ladin Band — Thu Sep 3, 7:30 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Thursday Live at the Odd Fellows At the Davis Odd Fellows Lodge September 3, 2026 The Evie Ladin Band Our shows are donation only. Your generous donations all go to the musicians. As always, our bar will be open to purchase beer, wine or sodas. Tenacious, innovative string musicians, the Evie Ladin Band – Evie Ladin, Keith Terry and Erik Pearson – throws down captivating, truly entertaining live shows. Grounded in Appalachian old-time repertoire, seasoned in African-diaspora roots, writing from life in modern cities, blurring the lines between music and dance, the polyrhythmic heat of Evie’s clawhammer banjo, resonant voice, real stories and rhythmic dance have been heard from A Prairie Home Companion to Hardly Strictly Bluegrass. Their performance experience is a stand-out. Doors open at 7p, show at 7:30p.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Common Threads, What Unites Us — Fri Sep 4 — The Artery
item.description:
Common Threads, What Unites Us is a collaboration between Lucy Boland of Bluewater Silk and Louise McGowan Bezark of Journey Vessels. The result is Lucy’s collection of reimagined vintage Japanese textiles and Louise’s fine art gourds. Lucy focus is on history and repurposing, and Louise emphasizes nature and transformation. This show celebrates craftsmanship, East Asian influence, tradition, and human connection.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Source: The Dirt
